reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis correctly invokes configurational entropy and lattice distortion as stabilizing factors, but it overstates their ability to suppress diffusion at very high temperatures (up to 1923 K) and neglects the well-known tendency of many equimolar multicomponent nanoparticles to phase-separate or form intermetallics due to enthalpic driving forces.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test is clear and uses appropriate in situ techniques (XRD, EDS, TEM), but the practical feasibility of simultaneous in situ TEM/EDS/XRD across the full 473–1923 K range under catalytic conditions is extremely challenging and not addressed.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a central question in HEA nanoparticle stability and proposes a direct, comparative experiment, making it a useful starting point for investigation despite its scientific gaps.
